<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**10** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3df08d268a42f629ecaf9131be585e8c86f14c43` — the merge of head `520a744547fd394936c89627da1289d9a1a21c16` into base `d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3df08d268a42f629ecaf9131be585e8c86f14c43 && git checkout 3df08d268a42f629ecaf9131be585e8c86f14c43
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663 520a744547fd394936c89627da1289d9a1a21c16 && git checkout -B drift-repro d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663 && git merge --no-ff 520a744547fd394936c89627da1289d9a1a21c16

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

review#1 (E1) takes this head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `520a744547fd394936c89627da1289d9a1a21c16`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.declared-row-not-moved-to-addition.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/suite-moved-overlay.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-environment-rows.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-served-overrides.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-overlay-merge.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts, .changeset/32606-declared-row-not-moved-to-addition.md, .changeset/32606-declared-row-semantic-entry.md

Face: schema (a `packages/spec/src/**` hit). Diff read against merge base `e540baf8`. Card #32606 and all of its comments were read.

### ① Derived judgments

- `ShipsName` becomes `{ item, name }`. Both moved-edit predicates now ask the address's package at the item grain (`ships.item(base)`) and the former owner at the name grain (`ships.name(former)`). This is the rule the module header on `main` already states ("the old owner must not ship the name and the address's package must"), so the code now matches its own contract.
- All three served-override candidate readers are swept. `findServedOverlayRow` and `listServedOverrides` read the name grain from `shippedArtifactsOf(type, name)` with no member, lazily, once per read or item. `listServedOverrides`' own "base no longer ships" guard correctly stays at the item grain. `mergePackageAwareOverlay` unions the non-stored, non-stand-in contributions of every slot of the name (`nameShippersOf`, built lazily, which is only safe because it is first called in the output loop after every push; checked) with the caller's `shipsName` for a list scoped to one package.
- The other two `mergePackageAwareOverlay` callers (the runtime-items merge in `protocol-meta-list-reads.ts` and `protocol-stored-collection-fold.ts`) pass no `installed`, so they never reach a moved candidate and correctly need no `shipsName`.
- The pins cover both registration orders for Z's address (valid Z item), Z's list, Z's execution list and Z's customizations. CONTROLs cover X's address, X's lists, X's customizations and the pair address, plus the #31593 CONTROL (X ships nothing of the name, so the edit still follows to Z) in both orders.
- All 71 check runs on this head concluded: 58 success, 13 skipped, none failed.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` is `minor` with `Metadata-protocol: semantic`: a changed meaning of which stored row a read serves, with no key or accepted value moving. This matches AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3. The ADR-0087 entry is `registered declared-row-not-moved-to-addition`, with no automatic rewrite. `@objectstack/spec` is `patch` with `none`, because the entry adds no key and no export. `Clause-②: no` is right. The card's fix shape suggested the `narrowing` arm, but no request the platform accepted is now refused; only the answer at Z's address changes. The `semantic` kind describes that more exactly than `narrowing`, so I accept the deviation from the card.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No governed path. The PR is authored by `objectstack-fleet[bot]` on the relay.
- N1 (nit): the changed rule also catches a member that moved alone: X shipped `en-US` and `fr-FR`, a later version moves only `fr-FR` to Z, and a tenant's `fr-FR` edit declaring X no longer follows to Z, because X still ships the name. The stored data is identical to the card's scenario, so the code cannot and should not tell them apart. But the changeset's BREAKING paragraph and the semantic entry's `surface` describe only the "bundle addition" origin. One sentence naming the member-alone move, and its fix (save a row declaring Z), would make the upgrade guide complete.
- N2 (nit): the Regime O shape (`isMovedBaseRowOf`, a row bound to X itself) moves the same way and is unpinned. One `it` mirroring the NARROWING case with a row bound to X would pin it. The changeset's mechanism paragraph already names `isMovedBaseRowOf`.
- N3 (nit): the unscoped list (`GET /meta/email_template`, no package) takes the `nameShippersOf` path only and has no pin of its own here. The scoped lists are pinned.
- N4 (nit, performance): `shipsName` in `readFlattenedMetaItems` re-reads `shippedArtifactsOf` on every call. It is reached only after `nameShippersOf` misses, and only for a moved candidate, so the cost is bounded. A per-name memo would make it read once.

### ④ Design judgment

`18.declared-row-not-moved-to-addition.ts` holds against ADR-0150 red line 2 (another package's customization is never served at this address) and D3 (a package that ships the name holds it), and against its first consumer, the upgrade guide. `surface`, `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria` name the moved reads and a concrete fix, and the tracker ids are kept out of the printed guidance (head commit). The implementing files agree with the entry. One row is served at one package's addresses only. The #31593 promise still holds wherever the former owner ships nothing of the name, and the read naming no package is untouched in this diff. No must-fix or should-fix. N1–N4 are nits and can be folded in or left. This is the final round.
